title: The Quiet Debt
premise: Ines Delacroix, a French-Arabic interpreter for a fragile peace delegation in Geneva, is approached by a man claiming she once saved his life—a favor she has no memory of. He belongs to a network that trades in secrets, and they hold evidence that the 'incident' she's buried—her testimony that doomed an aid convoy two years ago—was orchestrated by her own delegation's chief negotiator. As the summit nears, Ines must decide whether to expose him and shatter the peace, or stay silent and let the debt be collected in blood. She chooses truth, leaking the recordings at the closing session, then vanishes into the crowd as the man who returned her 'favor' quietly erases the trail behind her.
about_author: Lena Blackwood is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent six years in conflict zones before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped between institutions and their consciences.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Was
chapters.summary: Ines, running on four hours of sleep, interprets a tense pre-summit briefing in Geneva. Afterward, a stranger named Marek corners her in a hotel bar and thanks her for saving his life in Beirut—an event she cannot recall. He leaves a card with only a time and room number. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into dread; her carefully managed invisibility has cracked.

chapters.title: Insomnia Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ines reconstructs her last two years, cataloguing what she remembers of the convoy incident and what she testified versus what she saw. Her hands shake during a translation session with the chief negotiator, Anton Vidal, whose charm now reads as something colder. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the past pressing through the present; guilt recalculated as suspicion.

chapters.title: Room 412
chapters.summary: Ines keeps the appointment. Marek plays her a recording: Vidal coordinating the convoy attack to force a military intervention. He explains the network's rules—the debt is real, and repayment means delivering Vidal's private archive before the summit's final day. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: vertigo; the world reorganizes itself around a terrible new logic.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ines tests the waters, probing Vidal during a session and watching his micro-reactions when she mistranslates one word deliberately. He notices. That night she finds her hotel room searched, subtly, professionally. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she is also prey; paranoia becomes a skill.

chapters.title: What Amira Knew
chapters.summary: Ines tracks down Amira, a colleague from the convoy mission living quietly in Lyon, who confirms fragments of the recording but warns that the network isn't justice—it's leverage, and debts are never paid once, only refinanced. Amira refuses to help further. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: hope curdling; every ally is compromised.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Vidal invites Ines to dinner and makes his own offer: protection, promotion, silence—in exchange for whatever Marek gave her. He reveals he knows about her insomnia, her testimony, her fear. She stalls. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: seduction and threat braided together; the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Ines attempts a double game, copying part of the archive for herself while delivering the rest to Marek's contact. The handoff goes wrong; the contact is killed in front of her, staged as a mugging. Marek pulls her out of the scene. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fusing; there is no neutral ground left.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marek reveals the full truth: the 'favor' was manufactured—he chose her because her guilt made her predictable. But the recording is genuine, and so, unexpectedly, is his disgust at what Vidal did. He offers her a way out that doesn't include the network's cut. POV: alternating Ines and Marek. Emotional beat: betrayal and unlikely alliance; trust built on shared refusal.

chapters.title: Closing Session
chapters.summary: Summit day. Ines interprets the final plenary while carrying a drive containing everything. With cameras rolling and delegates assembled, she abandons her booth script and plays thirty seconds of Vidal's voice over the hall's sound system before security reaches her. Chaos; Vidal's face on every screen. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: climax—terror transmuted into clarity; the moment she stops being invisible.

chapters.title: The Quiet Debt
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Vidal is arrested, the summit collapses, and Ines testifies under protection. Marek arranges her disappearance to a coastal town where, for the first time in years, she sleeps through the night. The debt, she understands, is never closed—only carried honestly. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; truth cost everything except herself.
